rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice, especially for a mistaken understanding of a subject or fact.

example.english: I used to have the misconception that eating fish would never make cats sick.

rows.note: Use this casual expression when you want to stress that the idea itself is wrong.

example.english: The idea that girls cannot drive is a misconception.

rows.note: Use this for a general or established mistaken belief, especially in more formal or educational contexts.

example.english: The belief that staying up late is a rite of passage for young people is a misconception.
